## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Garudhammajātaka* (also referred to in scholarship as the *Kurudhamma Jātaka*; Ja 276) is a canonical birth-story preserved in the *Jātaka* collection of the Khuddaka Nikāya [Morris 1882; Sutherland 1991]. According to its opening narrative framework, the Buddha told this story while residing at Jetavana concerning a monk who killed a wild goose, introduced by the opening words “Knowing thy faith”. In secondary scholarship on narrative motifs, the jātaka is noted for its depiction of the yakkha Cittarāja, who appears as the ritual witness to an ancient rite wherein the king shoots arrows to the four cardinal quarters [Sutherland 1991].

Richard Morris observes that the metrical tale in Jātaka No. 276 corresponds in theme to the *Kurudhammacariya* of the *Cariyāpiṭaka*, where the eight verses of the latter emphasize the bare moral element of the story in contrast to the fuller jātaka narrative [Morris 1882]. In mainland Southeast Asian legal history, Burmese legal digests (*dhammathat*) cite the *Garudhamma Jātaka* alongside other major canonical texts to demonstrate that legal statutes were in harmony with sacred scripture [Williams 2005].
